deviation_mechanism: Broadband visible reflectance depends on alternating high/low index layers spaced at quarter-wavelength optical thicknesses to sustain constructive interference across 400-700 nm. As the gradient steepens, neighboring layers accumulate phase shifts that deviate from π/2, causing destructive interference to dominate the transmission window. This breaks the Distributed Bragg Reflector (DBR) periodicity, widening the stop-band unevenly or collapsing it entirely, which directly suppresses the objective score.
